open_points.subject: A9 — supported Linux platform
open_points.text:
The service runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named (owner, 2026-11-21). Another
   system, or a Linux or file system on which a call these rules rely on — opening without following a
   link, opening a folder as a folder, opening without blocking, creating exclusively, locking, renaming,
   flushing — does not act as Linux documents it, is unsupported
open_points.question: Which kernel, userspace, file-system types and versioned Linux documentation define the required behaviour and therefore the boundary between supported and unsupported deployments?
options: Pin a complete Linux deployment image and supported file-system set
Name minimum kernel, libc and file-system versions plus the authoritative documentation
Treat every Linux version and file system as supported unless a listed operation is observed to fail
open_points.default_guess: Pin the deployment image by digest, name its kernel/userspace baseline, and support only explicitly listed local file systems.

open_points.subject: A9 — meanings of the relied-on file operations
open_points.text:
opening without following a link, opening a folder as a folder, opening without blocking, creating exclusively, locking, renaming,
   flushing
open_points.question: For each listed operation, which Linux primitive and exact guarantee is required—for example whether no-follow applies only to the final component or the whole path, what kind and scope of lock is meant, when rename must be atomic, and whether flushing includes the containing directory and crash durability?
options: Specify the syscall or API, flags, scope and required postcondition for every operation
Specify observable safety and durability postconditions while allowing any Linux primitive that proves them
Leave the primitive and its guarantee to each implementer
open_points.default_guess: Specify observable postconditions and a reference implementation using openat2-style whole-path resolution, exclusive same-directory creation, one consistent advisory-lock mechanism, same-filesystem atomic rename, and fsync of both file and containing directory.

witness.initial: The configured photo path contains a symlink in an intermediate directory component, while the final file itself is not a symlink.
events: The owner requests a scan or delivery.
One implementer opens with a final-component no-follow flag; another uses a whole-path no-symlink resolution rule.
outcomes: The first implementation follows the intermediate link and reads the file.
The second implementation refuses or excludes the path because a link occurs anywhere in its resolution.
witness.observer: The owner sees the photo offered or delivered by one service and refused or absent in the other.

open_points.subject: A2 — deterministic stored bytes under A9
open_points.text:
With one library version one source gives the same bytes.
The service runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named (owner, 2026-11-21).
open_points.question: Must identical source bytes and the same Pillow version produce identical stored bytes across every supported Linux image, or is determinism limited to one fully pinned build including native codecs and platform dependencies?
options: Pin the complete image and native codec build and make determinism apply to that build
Require cross-platform byte identity and prescribe every codec/backend affecting the result
Weaken the rule to deterministic output only within one deployment image
open_points.default_guess: Limit the guarantee to a fully pinned deployment image and pin the native JPEG and image-processing dependencies that affect encoding.

witness.initial: Two supported Linux deployment images use the same exact Pillow version but different permitted native JPEG codec builds.
events: The owner delivers the same source image through each deployment.
Each implementation performs the A2 operation sequence and encodes with the stated settings.
outcomes: One deployment stores one JPEG byte sequence and its corresponding sha256 and size.
The other stores a different valid JPEG byte sequence and different sha256 or size.
witness.observer: The calling flow and Portal store observe different placement facts and stored bytes for the same source.

open_points.subject: A2 — authority for named-time-zone conversion
open_points.text:
otherwise it is read in the time zone of the `timezone` field of the run settings (A8), and so is
   `DateTime`.
The service runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named (owner, 2026-11-21).
open_points.question: Which time-zone rules and version determine the UTC instant for a camera value without an offset, including ambiguous and nonexistent local times?
options: Pin and import a specific time-zone database version
Use the time-zone database supplied by the pinned deployment image
Use whatever time-zone data the host Linux installation provides
open_points.default_guess: Pin a specific IANA time-zone database version in the deployment and use it for every named-zone conversion.

witness.initial: A camera value has no offset, its run setting names a zone whose civil-time rules differ between two time-zone database releases, and both Linux releases are otherwise supported.
events: The owner delivers the photo on the first deployment.
The same photo and settings are evaluated on the second deployment.
outcomes: The first time-zone database maps the camera value to one UTC photo_date.
The second time-zone database maps it to a different UTC photo_date.
witness.observer: The calling flow and Portal observe different photo_date values.

open_points.subject: A10 — security-review coverage of A9 rule 3
open_points.text:
The total review of `SECURITY_REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md` over States 0 to 2. Each applicable category is
owned by a decision above.
- files_artifacts: APPLICABLE; references: A1, A2, A5, A6, A8; affected: M01, M02, M03, M04, connections file, source folders, Portal binary store
- concurrency: APPLICABLE; references: A3, A4, A5, A6; affected: M01, M04, M07
- dependencies: APPLICABLE; references: A9; affected: image library, web framework, validation library, web server
open_points.question: How is A9 rule 3 represented in the claimed total security review: must A9 be added to files_artifacts and concurrency and must the Linux kernel, userspace and file system be added to dependencies, or is the new rule deliberately outside those categories with an explicit rationale?
options: Add A9 and the platform/file-system effects to every applicable category
Add a separate platform security category with an explicit outcome
State an explicit rationale that the new support boundary changes none of the existing category outcomes
open_points.default_guess: Add A9 to files_artifacts and concurrency, and expand dependencies to include the pinned Linux image, kernel-facing runtime and supported file systems.

witness.initial: A reviewer evaluates the new no-follow, exclusive-create, locking, rename and flush assumptions using the displayed security-review evidence.
events: One reviewer treats those assumptions as file, concurrency and platform security dependencies and requires evidence for them.
Another reviewer follows the existing references and affected lists, which do not include A9 rule 3 or the operating platform.
outcomes: The first reviewer reports the security review incomplete.
The second reviewer accepts it as total and allows State 3 to start.
witness.observer: The design gate and the State 3 author see different closure results.
